meta.title: Demo Script
meta.walkthrough: To record: 3-minute screen walkthrough of UC1 by the consultant before the SE hand-over

brief.summary: Brightline runs maintenance for 140 commercial buildings and loses SLA penalties because requests arrive by phone and email and nobody sees the backlog. They asked to see one request travel from the tenant to a closed work order, and what the manager sees on Monday morning.

pains.text: Requests arrive by phone and email and get lost; no single queue.
Dispatchers assign technicians by memory, not by skill or location.
Managers learn about SLA breaches from the penalty invoice.

goals.text: Cut SLA penalties by half within a year.

agenda.note: Out of scope for this demo: named in the hand-over as a follow-up conversation (Q2).

brief.demo_goal: Brightline loses SLA penalties because requests get lost between phone, email and dispatchers. At the end the audience sees one portal request become a closed work order without a phone call, and the manager spotting the outlier site on Monday before the penalty invoice arrives.
brief.focus: Brightline's full process runs from contract setup to invoicing. The demo covers intake, dispatch, field resolution and SLA monitoring; contract setup and ERP invoicing stay out (see Out of scope).

story.summary: Brightline's operations lead and the account managers who pay the SLA penalties are in the room. The demo follows one tenant request from the portal to a closed work order without a phone call, then shows the manager spotting the outlier site on Monday, before the penalty invoice arrives.
story.thread: No request lost between phone, email and dispatchers, so no SLA penalty that nobody saw coming
story.opening: Last quarter's penalty invoice, and the tenant who called three times about the same leak
story.close: The Monday review shows the one site at risk while there is still time to act

use_cases.name: Request to closed work order
use_cases.flow_line: Tenant reports a leak on the portal → work order created with SLA → dispatcher assigns the right technician → technician resolves it on site → tenant sees it closed
use_cases.summary: One request goes end to end without a phone call. It proves the single queue (P1) and skill-based assignment (P2).

items.bubble: Today a tenant at Harbor Point notices water under the sink in the third-floor kitchen. Instead of calling, they open the portal. Watch where that request lands.

items.text: Customer portal → **New request** → Category = **"Plumbing"**, Priority = **"Critical"**, description *"Water leak under kitchen sink, 3rd floor"* → Save → confirmation **WO-1042** shown
**Cases** list page → folder **Open work orders** → **WO-1042** on top, **SLA due** in 4 hours *(calculated by the service contract)*
Open **WO-1042** → progress bar on stage **"New"** → **Site** = **Harbor Point Tower** *(linked from the portal user's account)*

items.bubble: The dispatcher does not guess who goes. The system already knows who is certified for plumbing and who is closest.

items.text: Field **Assigned technician** → list shows **Marco Diaz** first *(filtered by the rule: skill "Plumbing", region "Downtown")* → select → stage moves to **"Assigned"**
Creatio Mobile, **Marco Diaz**'s view → **My work orders** → **WO-1042** → **Start work** → stage **"In progress"**, **Arrived at** filled *(current time)*
Tab **Resolution** → **Root cause** = **"Worn valve seal"** → **Complete** → stage **"Resolved"** → email **N-1** to tenant *(sent by the process)*

items.bubble: From the tenant's side, the loop closes on its own: no follow-up call, and the response time is on record.

items.text: Customer portal → **My requests** → **WO-1042** status **"Resolved"**, **Resolved in** = 2 h 10 min *(calculated)*

use_cases.entry_point: Customer portal (tenant) → Cases list page in the Service workplace
use_cases.value_message: Instead of a tenant phoning a dispatcher who assigns whoever answers, the request lands in one queue with its SLA and the right certified technician pre-filtered, which means fewer lost requests and fewer penalties.

use_cases.name: Monday SLA review
use_cases.flow_line: Manager opens the service home page → sees SLA risk by site → drills into a breach → reassigns with one action
use_cases.summary: The manager learns about breaches before the invoice does. It proves P3 with live numbers seeded across six weeks.

items.bubble: Monday, nine o'clock. The service manager does not ask for a report; the home page is the report.

items.text: **Service** home page → metric **Open work orders** = 38, metric **At SLA risk** = 5 *(work orders due within 2 hours)*
Chart **SLA compliance by site** → bar **Riverside Plaza** at 71% → drill down → list of its breached work orders

items.bubble: One site is clearly the outlier. Instead of an email chain, the manager acts from where they are.

items.text: Open **WO-1017** → **Escalate** → **Escalation reason** = **"Technician unavailable"** → stage **"Escalated"** → task for **Service dispatcher** role *(created by the process)*
Creatio.ai panel → *"Summarize SLA risks for Riverside Plaza this week"* → summary with 3 work orders and a suggested action *(AI skill "SLA risk summary")*

use_cases.value_message: Instead of learning about breaches from the penalty invoice, the manager sees SLA risk by site every Monday and escalates in one action, which means penalties are prevented, not paid.

ground_rules: All integrations are mocked: no live connectors. ERP data is preloaded; each on-stage 'system call' shows as a timeline note.
Extend the Golden Service copy — Case is the work order. Do not rebuild Service objects.
UI in English; on-screen numbers come only from the demo data workbook.
No JSON, payloads or technical IDs on screen.
One demo login (John Best) holds every internal role; only the tenant uses a separate portal login.
All dates relative to the demo day; run 'Run before demo' before every session.

_notes_research: Research blocks below are ILLUSTRATIVE — they show the shape. A real run fills them from the transcript, the web and SharePoint Custom DEMOs (references/research-playbook.md), with real sources.

moments.speaker: Dana Whitfield
moments.quote: Last quarter we paid eighty thousand in SLA penalties and found out from the invoice.
moments.insight: Penalties are the money story — the manager view must show risk before breach

moments.speaker: Raj Patel
moments.quote: Technicians need to see the asset history before they walk in.
moments.insight: Asset / equipment history on the work order — not in the agreed use cases

moments.speaker: Raj Patel
moments.quote: Dispatch runs on a Dynamics partner add-on we inherited.
moments.insight: Microsoft is the incumbent — expect a Dynamics 365 Field Service comparison

moments.speaker: Dana Whitfield
moments.quote: Every change request to our current system takes the partner six weeks.
moments.insight: Speed of change matters — show a live no-code change

moments.speaker: Dana Whitfield
moments.quote: We want to decide before the new contracts start in January.
moments.insight: Decision by December — keep the build focused

industry.name: Commercial facility management
industry.summary: Integrated facility-management providers run maintenance contracts with response-time SLAs per building; margins depend on first-time fix and penalty avoidance.

points.point: Contracts carry response and resolution SLAs per priority, with financial penalties
points.demo_implication: Show SLA due on every work order and risk before breach

points.point: First-time fix rate is the headline operational KPI
points.why: Repeat visits cost margin and tenant satisfaction
points.demo_implication: Add first-time fix to the manager's home page if accepted (PA2)

points.point: Planned preventive maintenance (PPM) sits next to reactive work
points.demo_implication: Mention PPM in a bubble; do not build it

competitive.summary: Microsoft is the incumbent through a partner add-on (D3); Salesforce is the usual alternative in field service.

competitors.name: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service
competitors.would_show: Work orders, scheduling board, Field Service mobile app, Power BI reports
competitors.strengths: Mature scheduling board and resource optimisation; Microsoft 365 integration
competitors.gaps: Changes go through partners and Power Platform skills — the six-week change cycle the COO complained about (D4)

sources.title: Battlecard: Microsoft Power Platform vs Creatio (internal, 2025)

competitors.name: Salesforce Field Service
competitors.would_show: Dispatcher console, appointment scheduling, Field Service mobile
competitors.gaps: Field Service is a separate add-on licence on top of Service Cloud; heavier admin

points.they_show: A scheduling board assigning the nearest technician
points.creatio_better: The skill-and-region filter is a no-code business rule the customer can change themselves
points.demo_highlight: After UC1 step 4, change the rule live in Freedom UI designer (add region 'North Hills') in under a minute
points.trap: Do not compete on optimisation algorithms — Brightline did not ask for route optimisation

points.they_show: Power BI dashboards built by the partner
points.creatio_better: Home page widgets are configured in the same platform by the manager's team
points.demo_highlight: Add a widget to the Service home page live

reuse: SLA risk metric with a drill-down list
lessons: The mobile step stalled when the technician's list was empty — seed today's work orders
